chapters.title: Israel enslaved in Egypt
chapters.summary: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt. A new Pharaoh fears them, forces them into hard labor and orders their baby boys killed, but the Hebrew midwives fear God and refuse.

chapters.title: The birth of Moses
chapters.summary: A Hebrew baby is hidden in a basket on the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter as Moses. Grown, he kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian and marries. God hears Israel's groaning.

chapters.title: The burning bush
chapters.summary: God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns but is not consumed. He sends Moses to bring Israel out of Egypt and reveals His name: I AM WHO I AM.

chapters.title: Signs for Moses
chapters.summary: God gives Moses signs to prove his call and answers his excuses, sending Aaron to speak for him. Moses returns to Egypt, and the elders of Israel believe and worship.

chapters.title: Bricks without straw
chapters.summary: Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go and makes their work harder, ordering them to gather their own straw. The people blame Moses, and Moses cries out to God.

chapters.title: God's promise renewed
chapters.summary: God reminds Moses of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and promises to redeem Israel with an outstretched arm. A family record of Moses and Aaron follows.

chapters.title: Water turned to blood
chapters.summary: Aaron's staff becomes a serpent before Pharaoh. In the first plague, the Nile turns to blood, but Pharaoh's heart stays hard.

chapters.title: Frogs, gnats and flies
chapters.summary: Frogs, gnats and swarms of flies strike Egypt, while the flies spare Goshen where Israel lives. Pharaoh bargains, then hardens his heart again.

chapters.title: Livestock, boils and hail
chapters.summary: Disease kills Egypt's livestock, boils break out, and the worst hailstorm in Egypt's history falls. Pharaoh admits his sin, then changes his mind once the hail stops.

chapters.title: Locusts and darkness
chapters.summary: Locusts devour what the hail left, and a thick darkness covers Egypt for three days, though Israel has light. Pharaoh drives Moses away in anger.

chapters.title: The last plague announced
chapters.summary: God warns that every firstborn in Egypt will die at midnight, while Israel will be spared. Moses leaves Pharaoh in hot anger.

chapters.title: The Passover
chapters.summary: Each Israelite household kills a lamb and marks its doorframe with blood, and the Lord passes over those houses. Egypt's firstborn die, and Israel leaves in haste after 430 years.

chapters.title: Remember this day
chapters.summary: God tells Israel to dedicate their firstborn and keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as a memorial. He leads them by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

chapters.title: Crossing the Red Sea
chapters.summary: Pharaoh's army chases Israel to the sea. Moses says, "Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord." The waters part, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the sea returns over the Egyptians.

chapters.title: The song of Moses
chapters.summary: Moses and Miriam lead Israel in a song of praise for their deliverance. Then at Marah, bitter water is made sweet, and God calls Himself the Lord who heals.

chapters.title: Manna and quail
chapters.summary: The people grumble in the wilderness, and God sends quail at evening and manna each morning, with a double portion before the Sabbath.

chapters.title: Water from the rock
chapters.summary: At Rephidim God brings water from a rock. Israel defeats Amalek while Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' tired hands.

chapters.title: Jethro's advice
chapters.summary: Moses' father-in-law Jethro rejoices at what God has done and advises Moses to share the work of judging the people with capable leaders.

chapters.title: At Mount Sinai
chapters.summary: God offers Israel a covenant: they will be His treasured possession, a kingdom of priests. The people prepare, and God descends on the mountain in fire, smoke and thunder.

chapters.title: The Ten Commandments
chapters.summary: God speaks the Ten Commandments to Israel. The people are afraid and ask Moses to speak to them instead. God gives instructions for a simple altar.

chapters.title: Laws on servants and injury
chapters.summary: The first of the case laws: limits on servitude, and rules for cases of violence, injury and damage, including the principle of an eye for an eye.

chapters.title: Laws on property and care
chapters.summary: Laws about theft, damage and borrowed property, followed by commands to protect strangers, widows, orphans and the poor.

chapters.title: Justice and the feasts
chapters.summary: Commands for honest justice and kindness even to enemies, a Sabbath for the land, three yearly feasts, and the promise of an angel to guide Israel into the land.

chapters.title: The covenant confirmed
chapters.summary: Israel promises to do all the Lord has said, and the covenant is sealed with blood. Moses and the elders see the God of Israel, and Moses goes up the mountain for forty days.

chapters.title: The ark and the table
chapters.summary: God asks for offerings to build a sanctuary so He may dwell among His people. He gives the design of the ark, the mercy seat, the table and the lampstand.

chapters.title: The tabernacle
chapters.summary: Detailed instructions for the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, frames and the veil that separates the Most Holy Place.

chapters.title: The altar and courtyard
chapters.summary: Instructions for the bronze altar of burnt offering, the courtyard around the tabernacle, and the oil for the lamp that must burn continually.

chapters.title: The priests' garments
chapters.summary: Aaron and his sons are set apart as priests. Their garments are described: the ephod, the breastpiece with Israel's twelve tribes, and the gold plate reading Holiness to the Lord.

chapters.title: Ordaining the priests
chapters.summary: A seven-day ceremony consecrates Aaron and his sons. Daily offerings are commanded, and God promises to dwell among Israel and be their God.

chapters.title: Incense, ransom and oil
chapters.summary: Instructions for the altar of incense, the half-shekel ransom for each person, the bronze basin for washing, and the holy anointing oil and incense.

chapters.title: Skilled workers and the Sabbath
chapters.summary: God fills Bezalel and Oholiab with skill to make the tabernacle. The Sabbath is a lasting sign between God and Israel. Moses receives the two tablets.

chapters.title: The golden calf
chapters.summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make a golden calf and worship it. Moses pleads for them, breaks the tablets in anger, and the calf is destroyed.

chapters.title: Show me your glory
chapters.summary: God says He will not go with this stubborn people, and Moses intercedes. In the tent of meeting God speaks with Moses face to face, and Moses asks to see His glory.

chapters.title: The covenant renewed
chapters.summary: God proclaims His name to Moses: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness. New tablets are cut, and Moses' face shines.

chapters.title: Gifts for the tabernacle
chapters.summary: Moses calls for the Sabbath to be kept and for offerings. The people give freely, their hearts stirred, and skilled workers are named.

chapters.title: More than enough
chapters.summary: The people bring so much that Moses must tell them to stop. Bezalel and the craftsmen begin making the curtains and frames.

chapters.title: Making the ark and lampstand
chapters.summary: Bezalel makes the ark with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table, the lampstand and the altar of incense, as God commanded.

chapters.title: Making the altar and court
chapters.summary: The bronze altar, basin and courtyard are made, and the metals given for the tabernacle are counted.

chapters.title: Making the priestly garments
chapters.summary: The craftsmen make the ephod, breastpiece and robes. Moses inspects all the work and blesses the people, for it was done just as the Lord commanded.

chapters.title: The glory fills the tabernacle
chapters.summary: Moses sets up the tabernacle on the first day of the year. The cloud covers it and the glory of the Lord fills it, guiding Israel on their journeys.
